findings.statement: A compact two-timescale reporting-history blend improves mean reserved-month count error over the frozen matched controls.

reliability.rationale: A two-timescale blend reaches3.51183complaints/month versus persistence3.65284 and flexible3.77217 on three held months. Small time coverage and later diagnostic winners justify partial rather than broad transfer support.

mechanism.rationale: Complaints are reporting events, not verified failures. Received dates in a revised snapshot do not establish historical public availability, and no fleet denominator identifies defect probability.

novelty.rationale: Known source analyses and standard mathematical/statistical families are disclosed. This review does not certify a new law or exhaustive novelty.

significance.rationale: Useful administrative workload reference with appropriate retrospective timing limits.

reproducibility.rationale: Native adapter, frozen equations, coefficients and compact evidence were inspected. Separate computational review performs numerical replay; scientific review is not experimental replication.

impact.rationale: No independent deployed intervention, measured cost benefit or external experimental replication establishes industrial impact.

reliability.rationale: All saved predictions and primary metrics independently reproduce from source-verified inputs, including unfavorable alternatives. Reporting counts have no exposed-vehicle denominator and are not defect rates; nonlinear burst alternatives and unfavorable regimes remain retained.
